sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rishiwa and Kizamani (Shuwa-Zamani [ksa]) Languages of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-024. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tumi [kku] is only named as a fellow Kauru-subgroup language (language list and sec. 8 classification paragraph); no Tumi data of any kind.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-70. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Tumi. Table 1 'Status of East Kainji languages' lists Tumi with status '?' and no source, where '? signifies no information'. The phonology section (3.1) is about Boze/tiMap tone; the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2019 [2020]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. 4th edition. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / ms. Entry 447 'Tumi'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 447: '1.B Tutumi 2.A Kitimi 3. Kaduna State, Saminaka LGA 4. 635 (NAT 1949) 5. no data. Benue-Congo: Eastern Kainji: Northern Jos group: Kauru subgroup. Source(s) Blench 1984'. No Refs line (no grammar/phonology/wordlist listed).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In J. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tumi appears only as a node in the East Kainji classification tree; no data.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2004 (and later drafts). The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Paper for the Hamburg meeting (Gerhardt Festschrift), 12 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Tumi. States 'Many languages, especially of the Kauru group, appear to have no material available at all'; the appendix 'arm, hand' table lists Tumi with empty cells among 'Languages for which no data exists.. to underline just how defective our understanding of this group remains'.

sources.citation: Temple, O. (comp.) & C. L. Temple (ed.). 1922. Notes on the Tribes, Provinces, Emirates and States of the Northern Provinces of Nigeria. 2nd ed. Cape Town: Argus. pp. 227-228 'Kiballo, Kinuka, Kittimi'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; a short ethnographic paragraph (location in the Guri-Srubu hills, farming, administration from 1907, religion, head-hunting). No language data at all.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stub citing Ethnologue only; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. (unpublished, 2016-) East Kainji / Kauru-area survey field notes (the 2016 Kauru trip covered Bin, Nu, Vori; any later visit reaching Tumi would be the first data ever recorded).

sources.note: Blench is the only linguist to have surveyed the Kauru subgroup; if a Tumi wordlist exists it is in his unpublished files (rogerblench.info is defunct; no Tumi file in any Internet Archive copy).
